key_insight: The paper shows that deep reinforcement learning can solve robotic arm reach and static reach-avoid tasks in realistic settings, but performance drops compared with simplified benchmark environments.
engineering_relevance: It provides a more realistic benchmark for evaluating robot manipulation policies, helping engineers test whether DRL methods transfer beyond toy tabletop setups.
method: Built a comprehensive reach-avoid benchmark for robotic arms with realistic, unsimplified scenarios.
Used the MuJoCo MJX physics engine and Brax to parallelize simulation and training.
Evaluated DRL on both UR5e and Franka Emika Robot environments.
evidence_signal: Reported state-of-the-art success rates of 96.1% and 98.8% on reach, and 86.8% and 95.2% on static reach-avoid for UR5e and Franka, respectively.
watch_item: Results are strong for the tested settings, but the benchmark still needs broader validation to confirm robustness across more complex real-world conditions.
paper_title: Learning Reach-Avoid Task with Reinforcement Learning: Vectorized Simulation and Benchmark
